note: A rectified street-panorama crop of one Amsterdam house front; the house in question fills the image.

upper_head.instructions: What is the shape of the top of most windows on the upper storeys of the house front in `facade` (the head of the window opening, where the brick or stone sits above the glass)?

criteria.flat: Flat heads: the window opening is rectangular with a straight horizontal lintel or flat brick arch above it.
criteria.segmental: Segmental heads: the window opening is topped by a shallow curved arch (a flattened arc, much wider than it is tall), often drawn as a brick arc above a rectangular window.
criteria.round: Round-arched heads: the window opening is topped by a semicircular arch.
criteria.pointed: Pointed (gothic) heads: the window opening is topped by a pointed arch.

top_storey_head.instructions: What is the shape of the top of the windows on the TOP storey of the house front in `facade` (ignore the gable or attic window above it)?

arch_present.instructions: Does any window or door opening in the upper storeys of the house front in `facade` have a curved arch on top (segmental, round or pointed)?

criteria.true: At least one curved arch above an upper-storey opening.
criteria.false: All upper-storey openings have flat rectangular heads.
